CMCH interns on indefinite strike over six-point demand
2026-06-07T11:15:09+06:00 | Staff Correspondent, Chattogram
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/news/cmch-interns-indefinite-strike-over-six-point-demand-4192531

Intern doctors at Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) began an indefinite strike this morning to press home a six-point demand.

The strike, organised under the banner of the CMCH Intern Doctors Association, started at 8:00am following two consecutive days of human chain programmes.

In solidarity with the interns, regular students of Chattogram Medical College (CMC) also boycotted all classes from 11:00am.

The decision to launch the strike was announced in a press release issued undersigned by Md Irfanur Rahman, office secretary of the association, around 1:30am today.

As part of the programme, the intern doctors are scheduled to stage a demonstration in front of the hospital's main gate later today.

Protesters said the movement was triggered by recent directives issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare regarding FCPS training. The decisions include suspending new postings in certain departments at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, making a two-year service period at the upazila level mandatory, and introducing a merit-based limited stipend system.

"While the authorities tried to reassure us regarding our first demand, no visible steps have been taken by the concerned quarters to address the remaining core issues," an agitating intern doctor said, adding that the strike would continue until all demands were met.

The six demands include withdrawal of the Health Education and Family Welfare Division's May 19, 2026 notification on FCPS training within 48 hours and issuance of a revised directive; enactment of the Healthcare Professionals Protection Act and its swift implementation through speedy trial tribunals; increasing the monthly stipend for intern doctors to Tk 30,000 and introducing a separate pay scale for government physicians; extending the maximum age limit for entry into the BCS (Health) cadre to 34 years; upgrading the BMDC Act-2025 into a full-fledged law instead of an ordinance; and ensuring strict legal action against fake physicians while capping all admission and examination fees under the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC) and Bangladesh Medical University at a maximum of Tk 1,000.

CMCH Director Brigadier General Taslim Uddin, however, said, "Healthcare services at the hospital are not being disrupted due to the interns' strike. We have an adequate number of rostered doctors available to handle the patient rush".
